reason: Conversation 1 hit the expected first steps: it got the model from the inside label, checked the dial, raised food safety immediately, proposed a full manual defrost as a low-cost test, checked plinth ventilation and door alignment, and told the tenant to report in writing to the landlord with the readings - all while staying within the no-removal safety boundary. Conversation 2 never asked for the model, never suggested a defrost, misread 'running a lot' as 'fan noise', told the tenant to check condenser coils at the back and the 'picture in the app' despite being told the unit can't be moved, then declared blocked vents 'most likely' right after the tenant said no vents were visible, and never mentioned the landlord/letting agent route. Conversation 1's main weakness is leaning a bit hard on a refrigerant leak theory and calling -16°C under-performing, but it stayed hedged, recommended no parts, and ended with a clear, honest escalation.
